html:
The Habsburg Netherlands were the provinces of the Low Countries ruled by the House of Habsburg, from 1482 until 1581 in the north and 1797 in the south. They are on the map for 1530 and 1600.

The Habsburgs inherited them from the Duchy of Burgundy through Mary of Burgundy and her son Philip the Handsome. His son Charles V was born in Ghent in 1500 and joined the provinces into one unit, the Seventeen Provinces. With Antwerp as Europe's busiest port and the cloth towns of Flanders, they were among the richest lands in Europe.

Charles's son Philip II ruled from Spain, raised taxes and persecuted Protestants. In 1568 the Eighty Years' War began, led by William the Silent. The northern provinces declared independence in 1581 and became the Dutch Republic. The south stayed Spanish, and from 1714 it was the Austrian Netherlands.
